proposals.impact: Unblocks daily content publishing, which has been dark since 06:08 this morning
proposals.observation: Two CI workflows failed in the last 24 hours: "Daily Blog Post" at 06:08 and "Funnel-Hack Digest" at 10:21. The content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published. With zero quiz sessions in 48 hours and no fresh organic entry point, the blog is currently the only top-of-funnel asset producing new traffic. A failed publish workflow means that single queued post has not gone live, and no new posts are being generated to replace it.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file, read the failure log, and apply the minimal fix required to get it passing. The workflow is blocked from the safety list so Fred cannot edit it directly, but Joel should pull the Actions log for run created 2026-08-01T06:08:16Z, identify whether the failure is an API key expiry, a broken file-path reference, or a schema mismatch against src/content.config.ts, and make the smallest targeted change that resolves it. This is the highest-leverage fix available right now because every day the workflow stays broken is a day the top-of-funnel stays closed.

proposals.impact: Restores competitive research feed that informs Joel's content calendar
proposals.observation: The "Funnel-Hack Digest" workflow also failed at 10:21, roughly four hours after the blog workflow. Two workflow failures in the same morning window suggests a possible shared root cause: a changed secret, a dependency version bump, or a third-party API (likely OpenAI or a GitHub token) that stopped responding. If the cause is shared, fixing the blog workflow may fix both. If not, the Funnel-Hack Digest failure means Joel's competitive research feed is also dark, which will degrade future content quality as the queue drains.
proposals.proposal: After investigating the blog workflow failure (Proposal 1), compare its error output against the Funnel-Hack Digest failure log from the same morning. If the errors share a common token or dependency reference, apply the same fix to both. If the errors differ, treat the Funnel-Hack Digest as a separate issue and resolve it independently. The goal is to have both workflows green before the next scheduled run so the content engine and the research feed are both live again.

proposals.impact: Money Vigilance open rate is 66.67% — highest of the three automations. Surface what is working in the subject line pattern so it can inform the lower-performing Money Worship sequence (37.5%)
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate across 16 sends, nearly 30 percentage points lower. Both automations were presumably written in the same voice, sent to similar segments, and are of comparable length. The open rate gap is almost certainly carried by the subject line, not the body. With the quiz at zero sessions, these automations are the only active conversion mechanism in the funnel right now.
proposals.proposal: Read the subject lines from all emails in the Money Vigilance sequence and compare them against the Money Worship sequence subject lines. Identify the structural or specificity difference: Vigilance subject lines that name a recognisable, specific tension (something the reader has actually thought before bed) will out-pull Worship subject lines that describe the reader's situation from the outside. Rewrite the weakest-performing Money Worship subject line using the same specificity register as the strongest Vigilance subject line. One subject line, one file edit.
